claims.text: Node.js is an asynchronous event-driven JavaScript runtime.
A project declares scripts, dependencies and devDependencies in package.json.
The engines field declares a supported Node.js version range, rather than proving compatibility.
package-lock.json describes the exact dependency tree and is intended to be committed into source repositories.
ESLint 10 flat config searches from each target file's directory upward for eslint.config.js, .mjs, .cjs or supported TypeScript variants. Earlier ESLint versions can use different discovery rules.

On GitHub Actions the workflow file lives in the .github/workflows directory, the actions/setup-node step installs the requested Node.js version, and the documented example runs npm ci and then npm test.
The same page says npm ci installs the exact lockfile versions and does not update the lockfile.

npm ci needs a lockfile accepted by the installed npm version. npm 11 accepts package-lock.json or npm-shrinkwrap.json. npm 12 requires package-lock.json and no longer reads shrinkwrap files. A manifest mismatch fails, existing node_modules is removed first, and package.json and the lockfile are not rewritten.

In the reviewed Node.js documentation, .mjs means ES modules and .cjs means CommonJS. An explicit package.json type controls .js files. Without a controlling type, syntax detection can treat an ambiguous .js file as an ES module. Detection is enabled by default since Node.js 22.7.0 and 20.19.0. Set type explicitly.
An exports field limits imports through package subpaths, so an unlisted subpath throws ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED. This is not a security boundary against absolute file access.
npm treats engines as advisory when installing a dependency unless engine-strict is enabled.
By default npm test runs defined pretest, test and posttest scripts, and npm run runs a named script with its matching pre and post scripts. Check script settings before assuming hooks ran.

In the reviewed Node.js 26 documentation, node --test discovers patterns including **/*.test.js and **/test/**/*.js, and TypeScript equivalents unless --no-strip-types is given. Confirm the actual runtime version before relying on these patterns.

Node.js 26 can run erasable TypeScript by stripping types without type checking. This built-in path ignores tsconfig.json and rejects syntax that needs code generation, such as enums. Earlier releases have different support and flags.
The release page says production applications should use only Active LTS or Maintenance LTS releases.

claims.text: Python packaging can use pyproject.toml. PyPA recommends a [build-system] table for build configuration. A [project] table holds package metadata, with a required name and a version that may be supplied dynamically by the build backend. Some backends use another metadata format.

pytest 9 supports pytest.toml and .pytest.toml as well as pytest.ini, .pytest.ini, pyproject.toml, tox.ini and setup.cfg. Its search starts from the common ancestor of supplied paths, or the working directory, and the first matching configuration determines rootdir unless a command option overrides it.
Ruff reads the closest .ruff.toml, ruff.toml or pyproject.toml with a [tool.ruff] section.
A requirements file, usually requirements.txt, lists items for pip to install.
python -m venv creates an isolated environment, and activation is optional when the environment's interpreter is called by its full path.

An editable pip install exposes project sources without copying them. Python source edits normally take effect without reinstalling, but metadata changes can require reinstallation and compiled extensions still need building.
pytest treats a run as CI when the CI or BUILD_NUMBER environment variable is set to a non empty value and then stops truncating the short test summary.
pip says regular installs, not editable installs, belong in CI systems and deployments.
A virtual environment is disposable, not movable and not checked into source control, and since Python 3.13 venv writes a .gitignore file into it by default.
By default pytest collects test_*.py or *_test.py files, test prefixed functions and Test prefixed classes without an __init__ method. Project configuration can change discovery.
Its good practices guide recommends an editable install for development and strongly suggests a src layout, particularly with the prepend import mode.

In pytest 9, pytest.toml and .pytest.toml take priority over pytest.ini and .pytest.ini. These files match even when empty. Other candidates need their documented configuration sections, with a pyproject.toml fallback when no other match is found.

Ruff ignores a pyproject.toml without a [tool.ruff] section and uses the closest configuration file. It does not implicitly merge ancestor settings, but its extend field supports explicit inheritance.
uv writes uv.lock next to pyproject.toml, a cross platform file that is checked in and not edited by hand.
pip lock is experimental, writes pylock.toml by default, and its output is only guaranteed valid for the current Python version and platform.
pylock.toml is the format PEP 751 defines.
ruff check reports violations and needs --fix to apply fixes. Fixing applies only safe fixes by default. ruff format --check writes nothing and exits with 1 when formatting would change.
